title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training
body:
**Title:** Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training
**Paper_ID:** 1502.03167
**Authors:** Sergey Ioffe, Christian Szegedy
**Year:** 2015
**Category:** Training Methods
**Source:** Arxiv
**Abstract_Summary:** Training deep neural networks is complicated by the fact that the distribution of each layer inputs changes during training. We propose batch normalization.

title: Attention Is All You Need
body:
**Title:** Attention Is All You Need
**Paper_ID:** 1706.03762
**Authors:** Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar
**Year:** 2017
**Category:** Architecture Design
**Source:** Both
**Abstract_Summary:** The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
body:
**Title:** BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
**Paper_ID:** 1810.04805
**Authors:** Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee
**Year:** 2018
**Category:** Architecture Design
**Source:** Both
**Abstract_Summary:** We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context. The pre-trained model can be fine-tuned for various tasks.

title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
body:
**Title:** Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
**Paper_ID:** 1910.10683
**Authors:** Colin Raffel, Noam Shazeer, Adam Roberts
**Year:** 2019
**Category:** Architecture Design
**Source:** Both
**Abstract_Summary:** We introduce T5, an encoder-decoder Transformer architecture whose unified design converts all text-based language problems into a text-to-text format. The architecture of the model -- its layer structure and attention mechanism -- is the central contribution of this work.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
body:
**Title:** Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
**Paper_ID:** 2005.14165
**Authors:** Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Mann, Nick Ryder
**Year:** 2020
**Category:** Training Methods
**Source:** Both
**Abstract_Summary:** We demonstrate that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, sometimes even reaching competitiveness with prior state-of-the-art fine-tuning approaches. We train GPT-3, a Transformer-based language model with 175 billion parameters, and evaluate its performance in the few-shot setting.

title: Efficient Transformers: A Survey
body:
**Title:** Efficient Transformers: A Survey
**Paper_ID:** 2009.06732
**Authors:** Yi Tay, Mostafa Dehghani, Dara Bahri
**Year:** 2020
**Category:** Survey
**Source:** Both
**Abstract_Summary:** Transformers have been the driving force behind many recent advances in NLP. This paper provides a comprehensive survey and review of efficient transformer architectures, giving an overview of methods that reduce the computational and memory complexity of transformers.

title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
body:
**Title:** Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
**Paper_ID:** 1409.0473
**Authors:** Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, Yoshua Bengio
**Year:** 2014
**Category:** Applications
**Source:** Scholarly
**Abstract_Summary:** Neural machine translation is a recently proposed approach to the machine translation task. We conjecture that the use of a fixed-length vector is a bottleneck and propose to automatically search for parts of a source sentence that are relevant to predicting a target word. This soft attention markedly improves translation quality on standard benchmark translation tasks, with the largest gains on long sentences.

title: Improving Neural Networks by Preventing Co-adaptation of Feature Detectors
body:
**Title:** Improving Neural Networks by Preventing Co-adaptation of Feature Detectors
**Paper_ID:** 1207.00580
**Authors:** Geoffrey E. Hinton, Nitish Srivastava
**Year:** 2012
**Category:** Applications
**Source:** Arxiv
**Abstract_Summary:** We describe a technique called dropout for addressing overfitting in neural networks.
